title: Swot Analysis of Django vs Flask
text:
A sleep and study habits project needs a simple website to recruit student participants. They need a site with a short description of the study, an eligibility screener of about eight questions, and a sign-up form that collects a name and email for people who qualify. Ideally, research assistants could also log in and see a list of sign-ups. Since site will hold contact information,security and privacy matter, and campus IT will want to know how the data is stored. The graduate student has never built a website, and the lab may re-use the website for future studies. The website will not be maintained full time. What would be a better choice to solve this problem: Django or Flask?
Simple Conclusion: Django would be a better fit.

title: Swot Analysis of Django vs Flask
text:
Django

Strengths

Built in security features protect your website from:

Cross-site scripting (XSS) protection
SQL injection protection
Clickjacking protection
Read here for more

Sanitizes user input by default (Cleans it to remove harmful elements)

Weaknesses

Steep learning curve for a beginner, since it is a full-stack web framework vs. a micro one.
A bit heavier than what the project requires (it only needs a simple website without much functionality)

Opportunities
Threats

title: Swot Analysis of Django vs Flask
text:
Flask

Strengths

Easy learning curve, since it is a micro-web framework
Ideal for smaller scale projects like these

Weaknesses

No built in security features, requires extra effort from the developer to protect against things that Django automatically protects against
Automatically trusts user input

Opportunities
Threats
